script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Hello, Chloe, have a seat. So, this is your review of the work placement at the city museum. How did it go overall?

script.speaker: Chloe
script.text: Really well, thanks. I learned much more than I expected.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Good. Let's start with the basics for the report. You applied for the education department, didn't you?

script.speaker: Chloe
script.text: I did, but they had too many students already, so I was placed in the conservation department instead. And honestly, I'm glad, because that's where I'd like to work eventually.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: And the placement was eight weeks?

script.speaker: Chloe
script.text: It was supposed to be eight, but the museum closed for two weeks in the middle for building work, so it ended up being six weeks altogether.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Six, OK. And what were you working on most of the time?

script.speaker: Chloe
script.text: They'd just been given a big private collection, mostly pottery and some jewellery. But my main job was cataloguing the coins. There were over two thousand Roman coins, and each one needed to be photographed and described.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Impressive. What did your supervisor say in her feedback?

script.speaker: Chloe
script.text: She was very positive about my research skills. She said my written work was fine too. The thing she wants me to develop is public speaking. I get very nervous in front of groups.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: That's a common one. Now, the report also asks you to reflect on the different activities you did. Let's go through them. You gave some gallery tours, I think?

script.speaker: Chloe
script.text: Yes, three or four. I'd assumed it would be easy, because I know the collection well. But it was so much harder than I thought. People ask questions you'd never expect, and you have to keep a group interested for forty minutes.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: What about writing the labels for the new display?

script.speaker: Chloe
script.text: Oh, I loved that. You have to explain something really complicated in about fifty words. I'd definitely like to do more of that kind of writing.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: And data entry? I imagine there was a lot of that.

script.speaker: Chloe
script.text: So much. And to be honest, I don't think it taught me anything. It was typing numbers from one system into another, and the new software could have done it automatically. I felt it was a waste of my time.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Fair enough, you can say that diplomatically in the report. Handling the objects?

script.speaker: Chloe
script.text: That was tricky. I thought it would just be a matter of wearing gloves, but there are rules for everything: how you lift a pot, where you put it down, how many objects you can carry. It was much more demanding than I'd expected.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: And the staff meetings?

script.speaker: Chloe
script.text: Hmm. There was a two-hour meeting every Monday, and most of it was about budgets and staffing, nothing to do with my work. I didn't really get anything out of them.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Finally, the school workshop. You helped run one?

script.speaker: Chloe
script.text: Yes, with a class of ten-year-olds. We let them handle some replica objects. I was worried it would be chaos, but it went brilliantly. I'd really like to run more of those if I go back next summer.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Interesting, because that's public speaking too, in a way.

script.speaker: Chloe
script.text: I suppose it is! Children are less frightening than adults, though.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: One more section. The report asks whether you'd recommend the placement to next year's students, and why.

script.speaker: Chloe
script.text: Oh, definitely. Though I'd tell them to ask for a clear timetable at the start. For the first week nobody was quite sure what I was supposed to be doing, and I spent a lot of time just waiting around for someone to give me a task.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: That's useful feedback. I'll pass it on to the museum, because we want to keep working with them. Anything else they should know?

script.speaker: Chloe
script.text: That the staff are incredibly generous with their time once you get to know them. My supervisor even let me sit in while she repaired a damaged painting, which wasn't part of the plan at all. That was probably the best afternoon of the whole six weeks.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Well, it sounds like a very valuable experience. Get the first draft to me by the end of the month.
